name: Window & gutter cleaner

pf.license.need: Usually none for window or gutter cleaning. Where the state's or city's rules require a business registration or license, the form asks for it.
pf.license.ask: The company's business registration number, where the form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Window cleaners need no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.repair_work: Gutter repair and gutter guards are home-improvement work, not cleaning. Some states require a home-improvement or contractor registration for them, sometimes only over an amount or on homes the owner lives in. From the state form; without it, those quotes aren't sent.
pf.license.insurance_bond: Liability insurance is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.not_this_work: Putting new glass in a window frame, roof repair and pressure washing a roof aren't window cleaning. Rope descent on tall buildings and lift work need a crew trained and equipped for it.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: a crew at the customer's home or storefront, priced by window count and stories, often repeating in spring and fall.

list.where: at the customer's place; an adult must be home for the inside windows
list.money: a card saved for the $89 trip fee; Rosie texts the bill after
list.weather: outside work has a weather limit Sam sets: rain all day or wind over 25 mph moves it, free

list.where: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be home

list.length: a day for the tall-ladder crew
list.where: at the customer's place; only the crew set up for 3 stories goes
list.money: a 25% deposit once the quote is OK'd, where the state's caps allow; the rest on the bill

list.price_kind: quoted at the visit, after a test spot on the glass
list.example: only the $89 trip fee is promised; the example visit: $245 (stain treatment $165, glass sealant $80)

pf.services.instant_booking: Homes up to 2 stories with a normal roof and under 40 windows book from the list. Taller, steeper or bigger homes, and businesses, are priced from photos first.
pf.services.capacity: A crew of two for inside and out on a full home; one person for outside only. A drop-off needs one person at the counter.
pf.services.nobody_home: Yes, for outside windows only, gutters and storefront glass. DONE with after photos confirms it. Inside windows need an adult home.
pf.services.not_offered: Glass replacement in a frame, roof repair, rope or lift work unless a crew is set up for it.
pf.services.drop_off_slots: Screens and storm windows are booked into drop-off slots by the shop's daily number, with no screen tech named.

words: a power line touching the house, a gutter or a tree near the windows
a gutter or downspout hanging loose
a wasp or bee nest at a window or gutter
someone fell from a ladder or a roof
what_happens: A power line touching the house or gutters: stay away, and call the electric company's emergency line, or 911 if it's sparking. No booking until the customer says the utility made it safe.
A hanging gutter: keep people and cars out from under it. Fixing it is repair work, quoted on site. The cleaning can still be booked.
Broken glass: keep children and pets away. Glass work isn't cleaning; the AI can look for a glass shop. Other windows can still be booked.
A nest: the crew works around it, or it waits for pest control. The note says which windows were left.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: Yes, for a hanging gutter, broken glass or a nest, with that part left out. No, for a power line on the house or a fall.

pf.first_steps.none: None for homes up to 2 stories.
pf.first_steps.photos: 3 stories, a steep roof, 40 or more windows, or a business: priced from the customer's photos first.
pf.first_steps.estimate: Gutter guards: a free estimate visit first, then a quote.
pf.first_steps.rope_work: Rope or lift work on a tall building: the building owner's written OK that each roof anchor is sound, before any time is offered. Sam gets it as a to-do.
prep_for_reminder: Keep the driveway free for the ladder truck
Unlock the side gate, and keep pets inside
Leave screens in: the crew takes them out

pf.visit.check_in: Someone home: the code at the door, entered by the crew lead. Nobody home (outside only, gutters, storefronts): no code; DONE with after photos.
pf.visit.walk_through: Before ladders go up, the crew lead walks around the house: cracked panes, fogged glass between panes (a failed seal cleaning can't fix), torn screens, where the power line comes in, and the wind. Photos of anything already wrong.
pf.visit.ladders: Ladders on firm, level ground, kept well clear of power lines, with stand-offs at the gutters. Anyone on a roof ties off first. No ladders in strong wind.
pf.visit.wind_on_the_day: Wind over the limit at the house: inside windows are done today, outside work moves to a new day at no cost, and it's billed once when it's all done.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: Add-ons only when the customer asks, priced before they're done. Hard-water stains are priced after a test spot. Gutter repair found at the visit is quoted only where the license plug-in allows it. A right to cancel where the state's rules give one for work sold at the home.
pf.visit.drop_off: At the shop: the code is given at the counter when the screen is left. Status words IN, READY. READY comes with a photo. Pick-up only by the customer or someone they name.
pf.visit.proof_done: After photos of each side of the house; gutters: before and after photos, debris bagged and taken away. DONE with photos when nobody's home.
pf.visit.breakage: Reported with photos the same day; the owner decides how to make it right.

pf.money.start: Window and gutter cleaning: a card saved for the $89 trip fee at booking, then Rosie texts the bill after the job. Pay by the link, the saved card, on the crew's phone, or cash or check.
pf.money.other_choices: Sam can set nothing taken, a card saved and charged at DONE, or paid in full when booked, per service. Plans: a card saved, each visit charged at its own DONE.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. A 25% deposit on a big job priced from photos, if Sam sets it. Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel or no way in: the trip fee (the example: $89), never more than it. On a job with a deposit (a 3-story home), what's kept follows the terms agreed, never more than the deposit. The owner confirms each one; no answer, no fee. A move for weather is always free, and no fee is even asked.
pf.money.drop_offs: Lee Screen Repair: nothing taken; paid at the counter at pick-up.
pf.money.tips: Optional, all to the crew. A tip line only if the owner turns it on.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes window cleaning, from the state form.
pf.money.emergency_prices: During a declared emergency, the state form's price rule applies.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking. A plan counts once a month.

pf.messages.photos: Photos of the home go only to the customer and the business.
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish. The crew's language shows on the job.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at home isn't the adult for the inside windows.

pf.staff.crews: Two on a full home: a crew lead, who holds the code and texts DONE, and a helper. One person for outside only.
pf.staff.heights: Each crew is matched to the highest home it's set up for. Only the tall-ladder crew is sent to 3 stories. Rope or lift work only by a crew trained and equipped for it.
pf.staff.licenses: None per person unless the state's form says so.
pf.staff.new_person_ok: Another crew lead can stand in, at the same time and price, if the customer says yes or doesn't answer by the evening before.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs quotes over the limit. The office manager may too; the owner's answer wins.

pf.rules.ladders_and_heights: Rosie's rule: no ladder near a live line, no ladders in strong wind, a tie-off on any roof step. Where the safety rules set more, they come from the plug-in.
pf.rules.weather: A weather limit per outside service, set by Sam. A move for weather is free, whoever calls it.
plans: The plan's terms show before any card: how often, the price a visit, when it's charged, that it runs until ended, and how to end it.
The plan gets its own yes, apart from the booking.
A price change is told 30 days ahead, or more where the state's rules ask.
Any reminder the state's rules require for a running plan.
pf.rules.add_on_at_home: A right to cancel where the state's rules give one for work sold at the home.
pf.rules.written_contract: Above an amount, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.gutter_repair: Lead-safe steps when a repair disturbs old paint, where the state's rules require them.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, with the before and after photos.

matter_most: Weather over the limit the day before: Rosie checks the forecast for each outside job; Sam keeps it or moves it, free.
Wind at the house on the day: inside windows done now, outside moved free, one bill at the end.
A power line or a hanging gutter: safety steps first.
Something breaks or was already broken: the walk-through photos show which.
Streaks: tell the business within 7 days; a free touch-up. Gutters that spill over within 30 days: a free check.
A crew lead out: another crew lead is offered at the same time; no answer, they keep the time.
Spring and fall plans: skip, pause or end, and a plan's price change.
A screen or storm window not picked up: reminders; after the free days, a storage fee only if the owner starts it, after written notice.
A gate code that fails when nobody needs to be home: the crew waits 15 minutes, then leaves; the owner decides any fee.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.
